findings.quote: The September 2, 2026 earnings release quotes Amie Thuener as CFO, so the finance role has changed hands since that proxy; the sources in hand do not say when or why.
findings.issue: Unsupported inference. The proxy's NEO list covers fiscal 2025 ("The NEOs, who were our only executive officers in fiscal 2025"), which ended November 2, 2025, so it does not show who was CFO when the proxy was filed on March 2, 2026. The ownership table even counts "All 13 current directors and executive officers as a group" as of February 24, 2026 while naming only twelve, so the change may well predate the proxy. "Since that proxy" is not on the surface.
findings.fix: Say only what the sources show: the proxy named Kirsten M. Spears as CFO for fiscal 2025, and the September 2, 2026 release quotes Amie Thuener as CFO; the sources do not say when the change took place. Drop "since that proxy".

findings.quote: The company believes such guarantees have a low probability of being called, and the fair value was not material.
findings.issue: Misattribution. The 10-Q's "low probability of occurring" belief is attached to "residual value guarantees, which are contingent liabilities we believe would have a low probability of occurring" that the company "may provide" under the AI XPV platform generally. The Backstop is a different instrument (a backstop of a customer's lease obligations on default), and the 10-Q makes no probability statement about it; for the Backstop it says only that the fair value "was not material" and "No amounts have been paid". The same paragraph also drops the basis of the $29 billion figure: the 10-Q gives it "on an undiscounted basis".
findings.fix: Attach the low-probability belief to the residual value guarantees it describes, or drop it from the Backstop paragraph and rely on the Backstop's own disclosures (fair value not material, no amounts paid). Add "undiscounted" to the approximately $29 billion maximum potential liability.

findings.issue: The 86% is total-company growth, which includes infrastructure software up 29%. The 10-Q credits the semiconductor segment's increase to "networking solutions, primarily custom AI accelerators and AI networking products", not to accelerators alone. The subtitle attaches a total-company YoY figure to one product line (the segment/period-mismatch trap).
findings.fix: Credit AI accelerators and AI networking, or reword so the 86% belongs to total revenue, for example: "revenue up 86% as AI accelerators and networking ramp".

findings.quote: Broadcom earns a BUY, though only narrowly. / a close call that the valuation section explains. / The rule derives BUY and we take it, but the margin is thin. ... so the call is close. / The call is close, because it depends on a downside weight that a reasonable reader could set higher
findings.issue: The close-call argument is made in four places: analystCommentary ("only narrowly", "A heavier downside weight would not clear it"), thesis, scenarioCommentary (twice) and finalRecommendation[0]. The "price asks for less than the Street's numbers imply" claim also appears in analystCommentary and again in finalRecommendation[0] ("the shares price less than consensus implies").
findings.fix: Argue the close call once, in scenarioCommentary. analystCommentary and the thesis can point to it in a clause. finalRecommendation[0] should state the call and its range, and not restate why it is close.

findings.quote: A handful of buyers take most of the AI output, those buyers need outside capital to deploy it, and Broadcom has begun to guarantee part of one customer's lease obligations to close that gap.
findings.issue: Cross-section paraphrase. The same three-part claim (a few buyers, they need outside capital, Broadcom guarantees part of it) appears in analystCommentary, in the thesis ("a few customers buy most of the AI output, and Broadcom now guarantees part of a customer's lease payments"), and nearly word for word in durability ("A handful of customers buy most of the AI output, they need outside capital to deploy it, and Broadcom has begun to guarantee part of that capital"). moatFactors[3] makes the Backstop-as-cost-of-winning point that durability then repeats.
findings.fix: Keep the full statement in one place, either analystCommentary or the thesis, and point to it elsewhere. In the moat section, argue the Backstop's bearing on pricing power once, in moatFactors[3] or durability, not in both.

findings.quote: Free cash flow does not deduct it and non-GAAP earnings exclude it, so both measures leave out a real cost to owners that is paid in shares rather than cash.
findings.issue: The GAAP/non-GAAP gap and the exclusion of stock-based compensation are argued three times: cashflowCommentary (above), multiplesCommentary ("the release's adjusted measures exclude amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets, stock-based compensation and restructuring") and risks.idiosyncratic[3] ("the adjusted figure excludes stock-based compensation"). Executive-summary risks[3] then points to Valuation. Several other claims recur the same way. The software Q3-versus-year-to-date growth and renewal timing appear in businessMoat.segments[0], growth.points[4] and catalysts[3]. "More than 20 gigawatts ... through 2028" appears in moatFactors[0] and growth.points[2]. Customer financing and credit conditions appear in growth.points[2], risks.idiosyncratic[2] and risks.systemic. The FY25 shareholder return ($11.1B dividends plus $2.5B repurchases in cashflowCommentary; the proxy's $13.6 billion in capitalAllocation) appears twice.
findings.fix: Choose one home for each claim. Put the non-GAAP/SBC argument in risks.idiosyncratic[3] or multiplesCommentary, software timing in segments, the 20 GW figure in growth, and the credit channel in risks.idiosyncratic[2]. Put FY25 returns in capitalAllocation or cashflowCommentary, not both. Other places should refer back in words.

findings.quote: Our view of the balance sheet is that it can absorb a slowdown, but not one that also triggers the Backstop.
findings.issue: The view is not supported by figures on the page, and it overstates the exposure. The Backstop liability is the gap between 85% of the amounts owed and what the racks fetch on sale, and approximately $29 billion is the undiscounted maximum after all racks are deployed. The page also shows $24.0 billion of cash and $13.7 billion of free cash flow in the quarter. Calling a Backstop call unabsorbable treats the maximum as the expected loss, and it contradicts the risks section's own mechanics.
findings.fix: Reach a view the figures support. For example: a full loss at the undiscounted maximum would be large relative to quarter-end cash, but the liability is net of rack resale value and builds only as racks deploy. Say what would make it hard to absorb (a default coinciding with falling rack values) without asserting that it cannot be absorbed.

findings.quote: The market keeps roughly today's forward multiple on the lower figure, which puts the shares below the $289.96 52-week low.
findings.issue: The scenarios are anchored asymmetrically. Base re-rates the multiple up to the low twenties on continued growth. Bear cuts FY27E EPS by about a quarter and starts pricing a Backstop payment, yet it holds today's ~18.3x, which is set on today's growth expectations. A scenario where deployments slow and Backstop risk is priced would normally also de-rate. Without that, the Bear looks shallow, and R of 0.59x sits just over the 0.50x line (the desk treats reward/risk just over 0.5x as fragile). The surface carries other checkable downside anchors that go unused: the Street low target of $215.88 and the 45.3x trailing GAAP P/E. The Bull is also loosely anchored. "Mid-twenties" on FY27E EPS does not reach about $530 unless the beat is sizeable, and "close on schedule" refers to a schedule the surface does not give.
findings.fix: Either argue why the multiple would hold in a slowdown, or let the Bear de-rate and re-weigh honestly; whatever label the rule then derives is the call. Anchor the Bull multiple and the size of the beat precisely enough for a reader to check, and drop "on schedule".

findings.quote: which suggests pricing power that is structural rather than borrowed from the cycle.
findings.issue: Contradicts the rest of the moat section. moatFactors[0] credits the custom-design advantage "with protecting volume more reliably than price". moatFactors[3] says buyers have "the weight to press on price and terms" and that the Backstop is "not a sign of pricing power". Stable gross margins across a mix that includes software and licensing do not by themselves show semiconductor pricing power, and the factor gives no counter-case (FY24 gross margin was 63.0%, and the sources do not break down the FY24 dip).
findings.fix: Reconcile the three factors. Either drop the structural-pricing-power inference and describe margin resilience as a mix/business-model attribute, or argue explicitly how pricing power coexists with customer bargaining power. Add the counter-case.

findings.quote: Two items temper the read. Cost of products sold rose to 24% of net revenue from 19%, as products, which carry the hardware costs, grew to 82% of revenue from 70%.
findings.issue: The paragraph does not reach a coherent view. The cost-mix shift is presented as tempering margins, but the 10-Q shows gross margin rising to 69% from 67% in the same quarter, and the report never says so. "As products ... grew" is a causal link the 10-Q does not draw, and part of products is upfront license revenue with immaterial costs. "Two items" is followed by three (cost mix, license revenue, tax). The tax sentence ("which the excerpt does not explain") only restates a figure without a view. growth.points[3] then relies on this paragraph ("The shift toward products and their higher cost of sales (see Financials) is why we assume no margin upside").
findings.fix: State that gross margin still rose to 69% from 67%, and say what the cost-mix shift means given that. Drop the causal "as" or hedge it. Either give the tax line a view or cut it. Fix the item count.

findings.quote: or if the fiscal 2026 10-K shows the top-five customer share rising further while fiscal 2027 consensus EPS is cut.
findings.issue: The baseline for "rising further" is not stated. The top-five share was approximately 50% for the three fiscal quarters against approximately 40% a year earlier, so a full-year fiscal 2026 figure above fiscal 2025's is close to certain. Half of the trigger is effectively met already (desk lesson: never state a trigger the current data already meets). The same watch item is also restated in risks.idiosyncratic[0] ("The fiscal 2026 10-K will show whether the distributor and top-five shares rose further") and catalysts[1], although triggers belong only in the final recommendation.
findings.fix: Name the baseline, for example above the approximately 55% of the fiscal third quarter, so the trigger is not already met. Keep it only in the final recommendation, and let the risk item describe the exposure without restating the trigger.

findings.quote: each tranche depends on financial partners whose appetite the risk factors tie to credit conditions.
findings.issue: The risk factor names "our customers and other AI infrastructure participants" and their "ability ... to obtain financings". It does not mention the financial partners' appetite.
findings.fix: Quote the risk factor's subject: credit conditions could affect the ability of customers and other AI infrastructure participants to obtain financing.

findings.quote: no source in hand explains the decline / the sources in hand do not break down the FY24 dip / The sources give no data on how easily a customer could switch / the sources in hand do not say when or why / something the sources do not name
findings.issue: Tic. A "the sources do not…" construction appears five times, plus three "the excerpt does not / cuts off / nothing in the excerpt" variants. The desk has flagged this tic before.
findings.fix: Keep the disclaimers where they change the reader's view, for example the price decline and the cut-off Samueli footnote. Drop or rephrase the rest.

findings.issue: The block is named "Consolidated", but its body describes the two reportable segments from the 10-Q, which the company overview says this report uses.
findings.fix: Rename it to reflect the content, for example "Semiconductor solutions and infrastructure software", or split it into two segment entries.
findings.note: Decline verified. lib/synth/merge.ts keys segment bodies by the FactPack segment name (bodies.get(s.name) ?? ""), so renaming the card would render an empty body. The body and the company overview both say the report uses the 10-Q's two-segment split. This is a Minor, so the decline is allowed.

findings.quote: Infrastructure software renewals, whose timing the 10-Q says moves that segment's revenue from period to period.
findings.issue: This describes a source of noise, not a catalyst, and gives no direction. It also repeats the renewal-timing point made in segments and growth.points[4].
findings.fix: Replace it with a dated, directional catalyst on the surface, or drop it. The other three catalysts meet the minimum.

findings.quote: the board's stated structure calls for a Lead Independent Director only when the Chairman is not independent.
findings.issue: The proxy says "there be a Lead Independent Director if the Chairman is not independent", so "only when" over-reads it. The sentence also reaches no view on what Mr. Hartenstein's departure means for outside holders.
findings.fix: Use the proxy's "if". Then either say what follows for holders, for example whether the role may lapse while the independent Chairman continues, or cut the sentence.

findings.quote: HOLD, with a $380–$470 target range over twelve months.
findings.issue: The whole target range sits above the $355.14 price, which puts the range's upside line at roughly +7% to +32%, and the weighted fair value of $406.50 is above the price too. The call is still coherent under the desk rule. The range has to bracket Base ($420), and the label comes from reward/risk of 0.37x, not from a lack of expected upside. But the report never tells the reader that the range describes the central outcome while the label prices in the tail. The final recommendation now states only the label and the range, and scenarioCommentary ends with "The $380–$470 range brackets Base" without linking the two. Read cold, a HOLD with an all-positive range looks like a BUY that was marked down.
findings.fix: Add one sentence, once, in scenarioCommentary or finalRecommendation[0]. It should say that the range brackets Base and the weighted fair value, both above today's price, and that the call is HOLD because the 39.5% bear-case downside gives reward/risk of 0.37x. The weakness is the downside, not the upside. Do not move the range below the price just to make the label look consistent.

findings.quote: Bear gets a fifth rather than a quarter because it needs both a customer pause and a de-rating.
findings.issue: The weight argument contradicts the rest of the case. The same paragraph says Bear "cuts earnings and de-rates them together, because a slowdown that exposes concentration and Backstop risk would also change the growth the multiple pays for". That makes the de-rating a consequence of the slowdown, not a second, independent condition that lowers the odds. The Bear driver also needs only one trigger ("a top-five customer defers racks, or a later AI XPV tranche fails to find financing"). The Bear weight fell from 25% to 20% when the Bear was deepened, with no new evidence, and this sentence is the only justification offered for the cut.
findings.fix: Argue the Bear weight on the likelihood of the slowdown itself, using evidence on the page, and make it consistent with the driver's "or". If the case for a fifth does not hold on those terms, restore the earlier weight and accept whatever label the rule derives. The label is HOLD either way.

findings.quote: a stall in the AI ramp would cost more than the upside offers, so the label stops at HOLD.
findings.issue: This is ambiguous. The Bull price of $530 offers more upside than the Bear's 39.5% downside, so the sentence is true only against expected upside (+14.5%), which is what reward/risk measures.
findings.fix: Say "more than the expected upside", or point to the reward/risk figure.
